\paragraph{Discussion and conclusion.}\looseness=-2
Across three architectures spanning distinct backbone families, our analyses consistently decompose VLA instruction routing into training-associated effects---exit collapse and counterfactual sensitivity emerging during VLM-to-VLA transitions---and inherited base-model priors (L1 attention routing persisting unchanged through fine-tuning).
$\Delta R^2 > 0.10$ provides a lightweight diagnostic detectable with linear probes alone; mid-layer features offer a principled tap point for downstream modules (reward models, planners) over final hidden states.
This cross-architecture consistency suggests these representational phenomena reflect general properties of autoregressive VLA fine-tuning rather than architecture-specific artifacts.

\paragraph{Conclusion.}\looseness=-2
Across three backbone families, our analyses consistently decompose VLA instruction routing into training-associated effects (exit collapse, counterfactual sensitivity) and inherited base-model priors (L1 attention), with $\Delta R^2 > 0.10$ as a lightweight diagnostic and mid-layer features as principled tap points for downstream modules.
This decomposition enables targeted interventions: practitioners can monitor exit collapse to detect under-utilized representations and route downstream modules to mid-layer features where action-relevant structure peaks.
The cross-architecture consistency of these phenomena suggests they reflect general properties of autoregressive VLA fine-tuning; extending this framework to non-autoregressive action heads and closed-loop behavioral validation remains a natural next step.
